quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low ground railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: Which action lowers the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.
Replace tires with bad tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on a layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: When driving at night with oncoming headlight glare, where should you look?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights—the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Is less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.
Is less pronounced when consuming wine instead of beer.
Is most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream affects your reflexes and judgment.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching you.
Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
Proceed carefully through the intersection, not always stopping.
Stop only for traffic on an intersecting road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a full stop. Give the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians in or heading toward the intersection. Go again when it is safe.

questions.question: To register a vehicle in New Jersey, you must be at least ____ years old.
questions.explanation: You must be at least 17 years old to register a motor vehicle in New Jersey. You need proof of identity and proof of vehicle ownership.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light at an intersection mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming next. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue carefully.

questions.question: Which action helps reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allowing extra travel time.
Obeying posted speed limits.
Using proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of travel time.

questions.question: What should you do when an aggressive driver is threatening you?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Retaliate by tailgating them.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make gestures.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers don't see other vehicles or when drivers do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers on the road to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about conditions on or near the road.
It helps direct you to cities and towns ahead.
It tells you about traffic laws and rules.
It tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell you about conditions on or near the road ahead. They are usually diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing on the left is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.question: What colors do warning signs use to show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs have black letters or symbols on a yellow background. Work zone warning signs have black letters or symbols on an orange background.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever you can.
Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to tell other drivers you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass another vehicle, the risk of a crash goes up. If you drive faster than traffic around you, you will keep having to pass others. Drive with traffic flow, stay within the speed limit, and pass only when needed.

questions.question: What is an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who looks at objects off the road or daydreams while driving.
A driver who makes eye contact with a passenger while driving.
A driver who only watches the vehicle ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching for things in your vehicle, reading materials, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and looking at your instrument panel often. These safe habits will help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: When can you drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are in the back seat.
If you are in the back of a pickup truck.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have any open alcoholic beverage in a vehicle on a public road. You also cannot keep an open alcoholic beverage in the driver or passenger area of any vehicle on a public road.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Take your foot off the gas, slow down, and ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas, slow down, and ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Remove your foot from the gas and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and turning slightly into the road's right lane. Check for traffic before steering back.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Honk your horn to make cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side and you cannot get all the way through. Wait for traffic ahead to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: What should drivers do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination quickly.
Drive closer to the car ahead.
Stay farther away from the car ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, you need more distance between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions hurt your driving ability. You may not drive well if you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad. Stress makes it harder to concentrate on driving. It is better to wait and drive when you feel calm.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slowly slow down and pull off the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas pedal and do not brake immediately. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street. This is true even if they cross against a red light or are being careless.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns of an upcoming intersection.

questions.question: How can you avoid fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: On long trips, stop every two hours for a short break. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and nap, or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes conditions less than perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive slower when the road is wet or slippery, when you cannot see well, or when anything else makes conditions unsafe. Even at the posted speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must immediately stop and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is being done on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
Keep the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never drive in someone's blind spot. Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving on the highway shoulder.
When your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves—you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: How much road space are motorcycles entitled to?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The full lane width, the same as other vehicles.
Half a lane width.
The sidewalk width.

questions.correctAnswerText: The full lane width, the same as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the full lane width, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: What affects how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down means you may use that lane.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not need to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: The traffic light turns solid yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop right away.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is unsafe.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless stopping is unsafe.
questions.explanation: When the light turns yellow, slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: In New Jersey, when is a driver under 21 considered to be driving under the influence?

options.text: With a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.01 percent.
With a BAC of 0.05 percent.
With a BAC of 0.1 percent.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 are considered driving under the influence if their BAC is 0.01 percent or more.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Protecting yourself by passing poor drivers.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Changing lanes quickly to avoid traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means identifying dangerous situations and taking action before an accident happens. It helps you handle aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers.

questions.question: You need to back out of your driveway and children are playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so children can hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check it is clear.
Tell the children to leave the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check it is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By staring straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check them.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. Continue to the next exit instead.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in residential areas unless a different speed is posted?

options.text: 10 mph.
25 mph.
45 mph.
65 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in residential areas is 25 mph unless a sign shows a different speed.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the road shoulder with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even if lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights on a two-lane road. Both directions of traffic must stop. The bus will have its red lights flashing and stop arm extended.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Under no conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean no passing or lane changes. You can only cross them to turn left into or from a driveway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign tell you?

options.text: There is a hazard ahead or nearby.
A school zone is ahead.
A public recreation area is ahead.
Food and gas are coming up.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a hazard ahead or nearby.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of hazards. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is beginning.
Pedestrians are likely ahead.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: The "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends. You can return to normal speed limits after this sign.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) is affected by all of the following, except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Physical fitness does not affect BAC.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
School zone ahead.
Construction work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency work.

questions.question: If your windshield wipers fail in rain or snow, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Roll down your window and put your head out to see.
Pull off the road to safety.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If wipers fail, slow down, pull to a safe area off the road, and turn on emergency flashers. Call for help if needed.
